key_insight: Optimizing both CTFO/BTO composition and sintering temperature maximizes magnetoelectric coupling in lead-free multiferroic composites, with 30CTFO–70BTO sintered at 1200 °C giving the best response.
engineering_relevance: The study points to a practical route for lead-free multifunctional materials for low-power memory, sensing, spintronic, and actuator devices.
method: Solid-state synthesis of (x)Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4–(100-x)BaTiO3 composites with x = 10, 20, 30
Structural and microstructural characterization using XRD/Rietveld refinement and microscopy
Electrical, magnetic, and magnetoelectric measurements across different sintering temperatures
evidence_signal: The abstract reports phase coexistence of tetragonal BTO and cubic spinel CTFO, improved densification/grain growth at higher sintering temperatures, and a peak magnetoelectric coefficient of about 1.28 mV/cm·Oe for 30CTFO–70BTO sintered at 1200 °C.
watch_item: The P–E behavior is lossy due to leakage from the conductive phase, which may limit ferroelectric performance and device reliability.
paper_title: Optimization of magneto-electric properties in Lead-free (x)Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4 - (100-x)BaTiO3 based composites
